spatial_frame.description: A declared coordinate system. One frame per world is primary — 3-D, world-fixed, and the only one that says what a step is worth — and every other frame reaches it through a chain of transforms, so conversion is defined in exactly one place (SPEC §4).

dims.description: How many axes this frame has. The primary frame is 3-D; a floor or a lattice is usually 2-D.

integer_only.description: Positions declared in this frame must be whole numbers; projections into it round half-up and are understood to be approximate (SPEC §4).

parent.description: The frame this one is measured against. Absent on the primary frame and only there.

transform_to_parent.description: How a point in this frame reads in the parent's: `p_parent = translation + scale ⊙ p_frame`, per axis. A negative scale entry is the mirror (SPEC §4).

unit_mm.description: What one integer step of this format's lengths is worth physically. The primary frame declares it and no other frame may, so a step becomes physical in exactly one place (SPEC §4).

units.description: What one step of this frame measures: a length (`mm`, sized by the primary frame's `unit_mm` through the chain) or a lattice index (`index`), whose physical pitch lives in the transform's scale (SPEC §4).

vendor.description: The robot vendor whose install this frame belongs to. A vendor frame is not a kind of frame — just a frame so tagged (SPEC §4).

spatial_frame.title: frame

spatial_transform.description: The per-axis translation and scale that carry a point from one frame into its parent. A 2-D frame under a 3-D parent embeds as [x, y] → [x, y, 0] before translating, which is why its translation carries three entries and its scale two (SPEC §4).
spatial_transform.title: transform to parent

values_axis_vector.description: One number per axis of a frame — two entries, or three where a 2-D frame embeds in a 3-D parent and the third entry is its elevation (SPEC §4).

product_lineage.description: How a cataloged product says where it came from: an ordered list, origin first, one entry per party that handled it. The motivating case is one product with three parties behind it — Quicktron manufactures the A5, Dematic distributes it as the DA50, GreyOrange integrates it into a site — which is one class with one set of capabilities and three names. options.description: The options this party applied. An option appears once, on the entry of the party that applied it, so the same fitting is never written twice.

product_lineage_entry.title: lineage entry

product_lineage_option.description: One fitting, on the entry of the party that applied it. designation.description: The option's code in the naming party's catalog — the same word as the entry-level field on purpose, because it is one concept at two scales.

detail.description: An open description of the option. It describes; it never restates or overrides the class's own numbers.

name.description: In human words, and required: an option nobody can name is not one.

offered_by.description: Whose catalog the option came out of, when that is somebody other than the party that applied it.

replaces.description: Free text naming the stock item this displaced.

product_lineage_option.title: lineage option

product_lineage_role.description: What a party did to the product. Closed, because the chain runs origin to site and two designations with no direction between them are a rebrand nobody can order (SPEC §10.1).

product_queue.description: An ordered path of cells with a discipline — the horseshoe under a station's safety cover, or one approach cell. The path is the admission: every cell on it admits an occupant, and a scenario admitting fewer states a shorter path. A path step must resolve to a live cell; dangling, removed or non-cell targets refuse the load (SPEC §10).

discipline.description: What entering the path commits an agent to. `no_reverse` is the point of no return the sequencing logic must respect.

source.description: Where the data comes from. Data files stay external; this names them.

product_demand.title: demand

product_induct.description: An INDUCT PLACE: where an operator puts goods into a carrier presented beside them. The same shape as `pick` and the opposite direction, and it carries no fields for the same reason (SPEC §10).
product_induct.title: induct

product_lineage.description: How a cataloged product says where it came from: an ordered list, origin first, one entry per party that handled it. The motivating case is one product with three parties behind it — Quicktron manufactures the A5, Dematic distributes it as the DA50, GreyOrange integrates it into a site — which is one class with one set of capabilities and three names. That is a live commercial fact rather than a join key into another system or source, which is why it is not `external_ids` (SPEC §10.1).
product_lineage.title: lineage

product_lineage_entry.description: One party's part in a product's history, and the options that party actually fitted. As-built, never a catalog of what the party offers: a world document is not a product configurator whose rules every consumer would have to reimplement (SPEC §10.1).

designation.description: The product's code in that party's own catalog.

options.description: The options this party applied. An option appears once, on the entry of the party that applied it, so the same fitting is never written twice.

party.description: The organization's name in words; v0 has no entity for an organization.

product_lineage_entry.title: lineage entry

product_lineage_option.description: One fitting, on the entry of the party that applied it. It describes and never rules: what a class can carry, how fast it travels and how big it is stay stated flat on the class, exactly once, so no capability is readable in two places that could disagree (SPEC §10.1).

designation.description: The option's code in the naming party's catalog — the same word as the entry-level field on purpose, because it is one concept at two scales.

detail.description: An open description of the option. It describes; it never restates or overrides the class's own numbers.

name.description: In human words, and required: an option nobody can name is not one.

offered_by.description: Whose catalog the option came out of, when that is somebody other than the party that applied it.

replaces.description: Free text naming the stock item this displaced.

product_lineage_option.title: lineage option

product_lineage_role.description: What a party did to the product. Closed, because the chain runs origin to site and two designations with no direction between them are a rebrand nobody can order (SPEC §10.1).
product_lineage_role.title: lineage role

product_param_decl.description: One knob's declaration. A parameter with no default must be bound by every stamp; leaving one unbound is a load error rather than a silent zero (SPEC §6).
product_param_decl.title: parameter declaration

product_pick.description: A PICK PLACE: where an operator takes goods out of an inventory carrier presented beside them and puts those goods into the carrier an HTM is holding out. It carries no fields — which carrier is held out is said by the `presentation_point` on the same cell, and what is picked is said by the order the carrier belongs to (SPEC §10).
product_pick.title: pick

product_port.description: A boundary point where things enter or leave the world (SPEC §10).

direction.description: Whether the world gains something here or loses it.

from.description: The station a source port draws from.

into.description: The station a sink port feeds.

of.$comment: SPEC §10 describes these entries as carrier-type refs plus a designation; the Dallas catalog writes a carrier kind plus a designation instead, and says why in its own comment. The entry shape is left open until that is ruled — see README.md.
of.description: What passes through, one entry per kind of thing.

product_port.title: port

product_presentation_point.description: Where a carrier is presented to an operator. v0 binds it to a serving cell by proximity; explicit binding is an open question (SPEC §10, §12.11).

attributes.description: The point's presentation geometry as Map Creator states it: the cell it names, the height a carrier is presented at, the robot class that presents it and the heading it presents at, the direction the operator reaches from, and whether the operator works here. The cell is the producer's statement and agrees with the point's pose; whether a point binds a serving cell explicitly stays open (SPEC §12.11).

bot_orientation.description: The heading the robot presents at.

bot_type.description: The robot class that presents a carrier here.

cell.description: The cell this point stands on, as the producer named it.

cell_unresolved.description: The cell the producer named, as it named it, present only where it names no cell the same document declares.

display_attributes.description: How Map Creator labels the point for an operator.

is_workbench.description: Whether this is where the operator works.

pick_direction.description: The direction the operator reaches from.

presentation_height.description: The height a carrier is presented at.

light_curtain.description: Whether an optical safety barrier guards this point, as Map Creator states it.

presented_entity_allowed_types.description: What may be presented here, as Map Creator states it.

presenting_agent_id.description: The robot that presents a carrier here, where the producer names one.

presenting_agent_type.description: The kind of robot that presents a carrier here, as Map Creator states it.

station.description: The station this point belongs to. A producer that nests a station's points inside its record, as Map Creator does, states it here, and the shipped `presentation_cell` lenses read it.

world_coordinates_unresolved.description: The grid coordinates the producer stated for the point, as it stated them, present only where the cell it names is not one the same document declares, so no cell can give them back.

product_presentation_point.title: presentation point

product_queue.description: An ordered path of cells with a discipline — the horseshoe under a station's safety cover, or one approach cell. The path is the admission: every cell on it admits an occupant, and a scenario admitting fewer states a shorter path. A path step must resolve to a live cell; dangling, removed or non-cell targets refuse the load (SPEC §10).

discipline.description: What entering the path commits an agent to. `no_reverse` is the point of no return the sequencing logic must respect.

path.description: The cells in the order they are travelled, named in the one address vocabulary a stitch pair also uses — never bare key strings, which cannot survive outside the entity that coined them. The list is what the queue admits on, so it is also what a policy overlay restates to admit fewer.

product_queue.title: queue

product_repeat.description: Instance i sits at the stamp's position plus i steps. The step is expressed in the frame of the stamp's pose and is deliberately not rotated by the stamp's heading, so a rotated row marches along the same world axis as an unrotated one and the two span the same extent (SPEC §6).
product_repeat.title: repeat

product_sector.description: A shapeless named grouping used as a selector for behaviours — explicit members, or the region beside it, or both. A generator listed as a member stands for its whole expansion (SPEC §10).
product_sector.title: sector

product_stamp.description: One placement of a template, optionally repeated. Expansion always produces an instance level, repeat or not, so adding a repeat later cannot silently rename every identity beneath it (SPEC §6).

params.description: Values bound to the template's parameters, by name. A value may be any JSON the parameter stands for.

product_stamp.title: stamp

product_station.description: A workstation: what it does, and which product it is (SPEC §10).

role.description: The product this station is — `easyloop`, `box_induction`. Open by design: a new station kind is a new template, not a schema change.

product_station.title: station

product_template.description: A reusable sub-world: internal entities named by local handles instead of UUIDs, positioned in the template's own local frame, parameterized where the product varies. A template ships its own internal connectivity, so a site author does not have to wire its organs together (SPEC §6).

entities.description: The entities one instance of this template consists of.

params.description: The knobs this template offers, each by name.

product_template.title: template

product_template_entity.description: One entity inside a template, addressed by its handle. Its components are read exactly as an entity's components are read anywhere else.

components.description: Read exactly as any entity's components are read. The authoring profile reaches in here too — see authoring.json's strict overlay.

name.description: A label for people. Not identity, never unique, never referenced.

product_template_entity.title: template internal

product_waiting.description: A holding pool. Capacity is simply its cell count, so it carries no fields of its own — the region and tiling beside it say how big it is (SPEC §10).
product_waiting.title: waiting

spatial_cell.description: A node an agent can occupy — the thing the traversability graph is built out of. Derived by a tiling or declared by hand, with the same standing either way (SPEC §5).

adjacency.description: The four neighbours a survey states, one slot per direction with an empty slot where there is none: the original form the stitches beside the cell are derived from, which cannot state a one-way lane, an impassable neighbour pair or a grade.

barcode_properties.description: The per-cell robot permissions Map Creator keys by the cell's floor sticker, kept whole.

blocked.description: Something stands here — a building column, a pallet — so nothing may occupy the cell even though it exists.

composite_attribute_list.description: The cell's second, list-valued classification as Map Creator states it.

conveyor_direction_attribute.description: The conveyor direction Map Creator states for this cell.

floor.description: The floor this cell's record names, beside the floor its pose's frame says: Map Creator states it on some cells and not others.

grid_attribute.description: The cell's classification as Map Creator states it, which the orchestrator recomputes for itself.

has_storables.description: Map Creator's `hasStorables`, as it states it: a number, or null.

legacy_grid_coordinate.description: The coordinate a legacy system recorded for this cell, kept because real lattices drift and the declared frame gives only the nominal projection. Data, never identity, never a key (SPEC §4).

location_profile.description: The location profile this cell names: the per-robot-model, per-heading permission table `traversable_by` is the flat reading of, kept whole on the profile entity. Map Creator states it as the profile's id.

location_profile_unresolved.description: The location profile id the producer stated, as it stated it, present only where it names no profile the same document declares — a reference whose target is missing, kept rather than dropped.

neighbours.description: The travel grade toward each of the four neighbours — whether a neighbour exists, whether a robot may move to it, whether it may move there loaded — of which a stitch is the ungraded, two-way reading.

runtime.description: What was happening on this cell when the producer wrote it down: the robot standing on it and why it is blocked. Live state rather than layout, carried so a consumer can drop it on purpose rather than lose it by accident.

botid.description: The robot standing on the cell, or none.

size.description: A hand-declared cell's own extent. A derived cell's is its tile; a declared cell with no size is 900 × 900 mm expressed in the frame's steps — the one physical constant the suffix purge leaves standing, because a default cannot be a step count until a document says what a step is (SPEC §5).

size_info.description: The four half-extents a survey states, of which `size` is the per-axis sum: kept because the sum loses where a footprint that is not centred on the cell lies. In the producer's own unit, millimetres for Map Creator.

special.description: Whether this cell is where a robot re-establishes its position, as Map Creator states it.

store_status.description: Whether a movable rack may be parked on this cell, as Map Creator states it.

traversable_by.description: The agent classes that physically fit here. Capability, not policy: whether traffic is allowed to run this way is `flow`'s business (SPEC §7).

world_coordinate_reference_neighbour.description: The neighbour Map Creator measured this cell's position from.

zone.description: The zone this cell belongs to: the e-stop and light-curtain domain a safety event pauses or blocks whole.

zone_unresolved.description: The zone name the producer stated, as it stated it, present only where it names no zone the same document declares.

spatial_cell.title: cell

spatial_charging.description: A robot charging point. A marker with no fields, declared individually or through a tiling's `derives` (SPEC §5, §10). This denotes charging equipment, not a generic idle destination; charge-state dispatch is a simulator policy.
spatial_charging.title: charging

spatial_exclusion.description: A rectangle a tiling leaves untiled: anchored at its minimum corner, stated relative to its region's origin, in the region's frame's steps. Each derived cell whose centre falls strictly inside it is removed — from this tiling only, so what a tiling derives is a function of the tiling alone (SPEC §5).

origin.description: The minimum corner, measured from the region's own origin. It may sit outside the region, which is how a carve-out authored against a whole floor keeps its geometry when it is written onto one tiling of it.

spatial_exclusion.title: exclusion

spatial_frame.description: A declared coordinate system. One frame per world is primary — 3-D, world-fixed, and the only one that says what a step is worth — and every other frame reaches it through a chain of transforms, so conversion is defined in exactly one place (SPEC §4).

dims.description: How many axes this frame has. The primary frame is 3-D; a floor or a lattice is usually 2-D.

integer_only.description: Positions declared in this frame must be whole numbers; projections into it round half-up and are understood to be approximate (SPEC §4).

parent.description: The frame this one is measured against. Absent on the primary frame and only there.

transform_to_parent.description: How a point in this frame reads in the parent's: `p_parent = translation + scale ⊙ p_frame`, per axis. A negative scale entry is the mirror (SPEC §4).

unit_mm.description: What one integer step of this format's lengths is worth physically. The primary frame declares it and no other frame may, so a step becomes physical in exactly one place (SPEC §4).

units.description: What one step of this frame measures: a length (`mm`, sized by the primary frame's `unit_mm` through the chain) or a lattice index (`index`), whose physical pitch lives in the transform's scale (SPEC §4).

vendor.description: The robot vendor whose install this frame belongs to. A vendor frame is not a kind of frame — just a frame so tagged (SPEC §4).

spatial_frame.title: frame

spatial_pose.description: Where an entity sits, and optionally which way it faces, in a stated frame. Inside a template the frame is absent: the pose is in the template's own local frame and acquires a frame when a stamp places it (SPEC §5).

heading_deg.description: Counter-clockwise from +x. An angle is not a length and takes its unit from no frame, so it keeps its suffix and may be fractional.

spatial_pose.title: pose

spatial_region.description: A rectangle in a frame, anchored at its minimum corner and measured in that frame's steps. Declaring one in a frame whose units are `index` is a load error: an integer lattice frame is for projecting into, never for authoring in (SPEC §5).

size.description: Extent from the origin. Each extent must be a positive whole multiple of the matching tiling pitch — no silent remainder strips (SPEC §5).

spatial_region.title: region

spatial_tiling.description: What makes a region a cell_grid: derive a cell per tile at this pitch, each carrying the whole component map in `derives` (SPEC §5). Tiling is opt-in per region — a real site tiles the strips robots actually travel, not its whole floor.

derives.description: Every component each derived cell carries, verbatim — which is how an area-level fact is declared once instead of per cell: these cells admit HTMs, these cells have chargers. A cell whose `derives` names no `cell` component still carries an empty one.

exclusions.description: The parts of its own region this tiling leaves untiled. A tiling states its own holes, so no other entity has to reach into this one to punch them and a hole meant for one tiling cannot take cells out of another that overlaps it (SPEC §5). Absent means none.

pitch.description: Tile size, which is also each derived cell's footprint.

spatial_tiling.title: tiling

spatial_transform.description: The per-axis translation and scale that carry a point from one frame into its parent. A 2-D frame under a 3-D parent embeds as [x, y] → [x, y, 0] before translating, which is why its translation carries three entries and its scale two (SPEC §4).
spatial_transform.title: transform to parent

structure_access.description: The junction between a run of racking and the region it is worked from: this run, that region, this face, these classes. Four fields are the whole of it and it derives nothing at all — it is a statement, and the SPEC §7 checks and the motion model are its consumers, which is what makes a world expand identically whether or not a fleet is layered over it (SPEC §5).

along.description: The region this face is worked from — a cell_grid where the classes that work it drive, a plain untiled region where they climb.

face.description: The face storage is reached from — the one place in the format that states a side. Where a relay stands is geometry on its own level, because in a rack | aisle | rack zone the two are opposite.

rack.description: The run: a stamp whose instances are the bays.

serves.description: The robot classes that work this face. Absent means unrestricted.

structure_access.title: access

structure_access_cell.description: The binding: the one cell an HTM occupies to exchange with this relay. Nothing is minted for it — it names an ordinary cell of the cell_grid the HTM travels, found by the binding search or stated by an override, which are the same component either way (SPEC §5).
structure_access_cell.title: access cell

structure_direction.description: Which way along an axis traffic runs.
structure_direction.title: direction

structure_flow.description: Which way traffic runs inside one generator's cells — a policy statement, not a physical one. A cell_grid with no flow compiles two-way: flow restricts, never permits (SPEC §5, §7).

then.description: Both of these rules run traffic a stated way, so the direction is not optional for them.

structure_flow.title: flow

structure_flow_rule.description: How a direction turns into arcs: `one_way` emits along-axis arcs the stated way only, with crossings to the next row still two-way; `two_way` emits every orthogonal-neighbour arc both ways; `alternating_rows` alternates each row, even rows running the stated way (SPEC §5).
structure_flow_rule.title: flow rule

structure_level.description: One entry of a rack's `levels`: a height, and either the relays that protrude from it or the storage it holds — never both. An entry carrying `positions` is a relay level; one without is a storage level; and both key forms index the full list, so inserting a relay level renumbers nothing (SPEC §5).

height.description: How far above the floor at the rack's pose this shelf sits.

positions.description: Where this level's shelves stand, each an `[along, out]` offset from the bay's origin corner in the bay's own frame. Which side of the steel a shelf protrudes on is the second number — at or below zero for the low-`y` face, at or beyond the footprint's depth for the high-`y` one — so the side is geometry and not an enum. Stating them is what makes this a relay level.

reach.description: How far from a relay of this level a cell may sit and still be the one it binds. A radius around the shelf: the binding search asks proximity and nothing else.

then.description: The offsets place the shelves on their own, but nothing says how far one may reach for a cell, so a relay level states a reach.

structure_level.title: level

structure_rack.description: One bay of racking: pure steel, and nothing about who serves it. Its vertical truth is one enumerated list of levels, bottom-up, because real bays are not uniformly spaced and a nominal pitch would be a second number that could disagree with the survey. It derives one relay per position of every relay level and one slot per storage position. A rack reachable from both sides is one rack with two accesses, not two logical racks (SPEC §5).

footprint.description: Extent at heading 0, anchored with its minimum corner at the rack's pose (SPEC §5).

levels.description: Every shelf this bay has, enumerated bottom-up. Heights increase down the list, and a list that does not increase is a load error: `the lowest level` and `level 3` both have to mean one thing. There is no level pitch and no level count (SPEC §5).

slot_pitch.description: Along-face and depth spacing of storage positions.

slots_deep.description: How deep storage goes from the access face — 2 is double-deep, where the rear position is reachable only after the front carrier moves.

structure_rack.title: rack

structure_relay.description: One handoff shelf, where carriers change hands between the rack system and the floor. It names the rack and the level it stands on, how high that is and where on the bay it sits — not the cell somebody stands on, which is the `access_cell` beside it (SPEC §5).

index.description: Which of that level's positions this is, in the order they are written.

level.description: Which entry of the rack's `levels` this shelf stands on, zero-based.

offset.description: The entry of its level's `positions` that derived it: `[along, out]` from the bay's origin corner, in the bay's own frame. An offset, not a world position — the rack's pose carries it into a frame.

structure_relay.title: relay

structure_side.description: Which face of a bay is meant, stated in the run template's own frame; the stamp's heading turns it like all stamped geometry. Only an access states one.
structure_side.title: side

structure_slot.description: One storage position of a rack, individually addressable so a stored carrier, a damaged position, or a double-deep front/rear pair can be named. Depth counts from the access face, which is what makes front and rear mean anything (SPEC §5).

col.description: Storage column across the face, zero-based.

depth.description: How far back from the access face, zero-based.

level.description: Which entry of the rack's `levels` this shelf is, zero-based.

structure_slot.title: slot

structure_stitch.description: A declared linking rule between two expansions' cells. Nothing links without one — two cell_grids that touch are two cell_grids that touch, never an implicit merge (SPEC §5).

a.description: One endpoint. Any entity whose expansion contributes cells will do — a region, a stamp.

pairs.$comment: Not `required` when the rule is explicit, because the reader does not require it either: an explicit stitch with no pairs silently links nothing there. Raised as an open question in README.md rather than settled here.
pairs.description: The cells an explicit rule links, two per pair, in the one address vocabulary a queue path also uses.

tolerance.description: How far apart two cells may be and still be linked by a contact rule; overlap counts as zero.

structure_stitch.title: stitch

structure_stitch_rule.description: How the two endpoints' cells are matched: `contact` links each cell of the smaller expansion to its nearest partner within tolerance, many-to-one by design; `explicit` links exactly the stated pairs, used where contact would be wrong — a station's only legal entry, a threshold, a directional gate (SPEC §5).
structure_stitch_rule.title: stitch rule

structure_storage.description: What a rack or buffer may hold. Two racks of identical steel differ only in this: the order buffer is the inventory rack template with `holds` replaced (SPEC §10).

carrier_type.description: The carrier type this storage takes, where it takes only one.

holds.description: Which side of the operation this steel serves.

structure_storage.title: storage

values_axis_vector.description: One number per axis of a frame — two entries, or three where a 2-D frame embeds in a 3-D parent and the third entry is its elevation (SPEC §4).
values_axis_vector.title: axis vector

values_cell_address.description: How anything names one cell: by its own identity — a declared cell's UUID or a derived cell's address, the two being equally valid here — by that derived address written in its two parts, or, inside a template only, by a local one. Never a bare key string, which would only mean something to whichever entity coined it (SPEC §3).
values_cell_address.title: cell address

values_coord.description: One axis of a position, in the steps of the frame that states it (SPEC §5).
values_coord.title: coordinate

values_coord_pair.description: Two coordinates in the frame of whatever states them, x then y.
values_coord_pair.title: coordinate pair

values_count.description: How many of something, zero included.
values_count.title: count

values_count_positive.description: How many of something, where none of it would be meaningless.
values_count_positive.title: positive count

values_declared_entity_id.description: The identity of an entity somebody wrote down: a freshly minted UUID meaning nothing but "this one" (SPEC §3). This is the one identity in the format that is a real UUID.
values_declared_entity_id.title: declared entity id

values_derivation_address.description: The complete address of one derived entity, in the two parts a record writes it in: the declared generator the chain starts at, and the key that walks down from it. This is the same identity `derived_entity_id` spells flat, and a record addresses a derived entity by it (SPEC §3).
values_derivation_address.title: derivation address

values_derivation_key.description: The `/`-joined chain of segments naming one derived entity beneath its generator. Every segment carries a reserved prefix and a non-empty payload; a payload keeps its own colons, so `local:present:0` is the handle `present:0` (SPEC §3).
values_derivation_key.title: derivation key

values_derived_entity_id.description: The identity of an entity a generator produced: the address it was produced at — the declared generator's UUID, then the `/`-joined key that walks down to it, `6f1c…/instance:2/relay:1,0`. The address IS the identity, with nothing computed underneath it; two implementations name the same entity because they walked the same chain (SPEC §3). This is the flat spelling, which is what an `id` field and a database key hold; `derivation_address` below is the same address written in the two parts a record addresses one by.
values_derived_entity_id.title: derived entity id

values_entity_id.description: The identity of one entity, either way it was minted: a UUID for a declared entity, a derivation address for a derived one. The two arms record HOW a name came about and never a kind of entity — derivation is a convenience and never a second class of existence (SPEC §1, §3) — so every field that names an entity takes either arm, and nothing may treat one differently once it has resolved it.
values_entity_id.title: entity id

values_entity_ref.description: A pointer at another entity: an identity out in the world — a declared entity's UUID or a derived entity's address, either is valid here — and a local handle inside a template. A dangling one is a load error, never a best-effort match (SPEC §2).
values_entity_ref.title: entity reference

values_flag.description: A yes-or-no fact about an entity.
values_flag.title: flag

values_local_derivation_address.description: A derivation address written inside a template, where the generator is still a handle; expansion rewrites it into a plain derivation address (SPEC §3).
values_local_derivation_address.title: local derivation address

values_local_handle.description: A template-internal entity's name, standing in for an identity until a stamp mints one. `/` is forbidden inside it because `/` joins derivation key segments (SPEC §3).
values_local_handle.title: local handle

values_local_ref.description: How one template internal names another before either has an identity; expansion rewrites it to the stamped identity (SPEC §2).
values_local_ref.title: local reference

values_param_ref.description: A template parameter standing where a value goes; substitution replaces the whole object with the bound value, preserving its JSON type (SPEC §6). Partial-string interpolation does not exist.
values_param_ref.title: parameter reference

values_position.description: A point in a frame: two entries in a 2-D frame, three in a 3-D one (SPEC §4).
values_position.title: position

values_steps.description: A length: an integer count of the steps of the frame it is stated in. Only the primary frame's `unit_mm` says what a step is worth, which is why no length field carries a unit in its name any more (SPEC §5).
values_steps.title: steps

values_steps_list.description: Lengths in a stated order, as many as the thing has.
values_steps_list.title: step list

values_steps_pair.description: Two lengths, x then y, in the steps of the frame that states them.
values_steps_pair.title: step pair

values_steps_pair_list.description: Offsets in a stated order, each a pair of lengths in the steps of the frame that states them.
values_steps_pair_list.title: step pair list

values_steps_pair_positive.description: Two lengths that must both exceed zero: a size, a pitch, a footprint.
values_steps_pair_positive.title: positive step pair

values_steps_positive.description: A length that must be greater than zero: an extent, a pitch, a footprint side.
values_steps_positive.title: positive steps

values_unit_mm.description: What one integer step is worth physically — the only fractional number a geometry document carries, declared by the primary frame and by no other (SPEC §4, §5). 0.1 is the expected site default, because source drawings carry tenths of a millimetre and a tenth is finer than anything a warehouse holds to.
values_unit_mm.title: step size in millimetres

values_uuid.description: A UUID in the hyphenated form. SPEC §3 writes identities lowercase; a reader accepts either case, so this does too.
values_uuid.title: UUID

schema.description: A reusable sub-world: internal entities named by local handles instead of UUIDs, positioned in the template's own local frame, parameterized where the product varies. A template ships its own internal connectivity, so a site author does not have to wire its organs together (SPEC §6).

entities.description: The entities one instance of this template consists of.

params.description: The knobs this template offers, each by name.

schema.title: template

components_set.description: An entity's components, read the way SPEC §9 requires a consumer to read them: a name this version knows must have the right shape, a name it does not know is carried and ignored. That is what lets one team attach a component without negotiating with every other consumer.
components_set.title: component map (lenient)

fleet_assignment.description: Where a cohort's robots may work. `hard` means they never leave the listed entities; anything else leaves them free (SPEC §7 — the validator warns when a hard assignment sends a class somewhere it cannot go).

kind.description: How binding the assignment is. `hard` and `free` are the values in use; the reader treats anything that is not `hard` as free, so this is not closed.

to.description: The sectors or regions a hard assignment confines the robots to.

fleet_assignment.title: assignment

fleet_carrier.description: One carrier: its type, the pool that minted it, its permanent designation and where it sits. Derived by a pool or declared by hand, with the same standing either way (SPEC §10).

index.description: Which of the pool's carriers this is, zero-based.

fleet_carrier.title: carrier

fleet_carrier_pool.description: A population of carriers of one type, all carrying one permanent designation, placed by one rule; a generator of individually addressable carrier entities (SPEC §10).
fleet_carrier_pool.title: carrier pool

fleet_cohort.description: N robots of one class plus an assignment policy; a generator of individually addressable robot entities (SPEC §10).
fleet_cohort.title: cohort

fleet_designation.description: Which side of the operation a carrier belongs to, permanently — a per-carrier fact rather than a per-type one, which is the anti-starvation ruling (SPEC §10).
fleet_designation.title: designation

fleet_placement.description: Where a pool's carriers start. The rule names the scheme — a sector, storage spread across the site, named slots — and the fields the scheme needs ride alongside it, which is why this object is not closed (SPEC §10).

kind.description: Which placement scheme applies. `sector` and `distributed_storage` are in use; the third scheme SPEC §10 names, placement into named slots, has no spelling pinned yet, so this is not closed.

fleet_placement.title: placement

fleet_robot.description: One robot: which class it is, which cohort minted it, and where it may work. Derived by a cohort or declared by hand, with the same standing either way (SPEC §10).

index.description: Which of the cohort's robots this is, zero-based.

fleet_robot.title: robot

fleet_robot_class.description: A kind of robot, distinguished by configuration as well as model: two robots on one chassis with different end effectors are two classes, because what they can carry differs. Who made it and who rebranded it ride in `lineage` — a rebrand is a party and a role, not a join key into another system or source (SPEC §10, §10.1).

carries.description: The carrier kinds this class can take.

configuration.description: What distinguishes this build of the model — the end effector, the carrier fitment.

height.description: Overall height, checked against the lowest level of any rack whose footprint a cell_grid admitting this class crosses (SPEC §7).

locomotion.description: How the class gets about: `floor` drives on cell_grids, `ladder` climbs the racking and needs no cells beneath it. Absent reads as `floor` — the exception is the one that has to be declared (SPEC §5).

native_frame.description: The vendor frame this class's own software speaks in.

role.description: What this class does in the operation. `htm` and `vtm` are the values in use; the field is deliberately open, because a human operator is a future role rather than a new mechanism.

fleet_robot_class.title: robot class

additionalProperties.$comment: Property names are unconstrained: a naming system is whatever the other system is called, and a legacy name is not ours to spell. The values are constrained, because a value you cannot join on is not an external id.
additionalProperties.description: Whatever that system stores under that name — a number, a string, a flag. Never an object: an external id is a value to join on.

identity_external_ids.description: The identifiers other systems and sources know this entity by — a legacy system's, or a site template's key for what made it — carried as data: joinable, indexable, convertible, never identity, and never a reference target. This is how a conversion keeps a visible 1:1 with its source without reopening the string-identity door (SPEC §2).
identity_external_ids.title: external ids

product_carrier_type.description: A kind of thing that rides an agent and holds merchandise. Inventory-versus-order is a per-carrier designation, not a different type (SPEC §10).

kind.description: Which physical kind this is. A tray is a tote without walls; a box is its own carrier.

self_carrying.description: The thing rides an agent directly, with no tray beneath it.

product_carrier_type.title: carrier type

product_demand.description: A workload source bound into a scenario: what the world is asked to do, and where the data saying so lives (SPEC §10).

kind.description: Which direction of work this source produces.

source.description: Where the data comes from. Data files stay external; this names them.

product_demand.title: demand

product_induct.description: An INDUCT PLACE: where an operator puts goods into a carrier presented beside them. The same shape as `pick` and the opposite direction, and it carries no fields for the same reason (SPEC §10).
product_induct.title: induct

product_lineage.description: How a cataloged product says where it came from: an ordered list, origin first, one entry per party that handled it. The motivating case is one product with three parties behind it — Quicktron manufactures the A5, Dematic distributes it as the DA50, GreyOrange integrates it into a site — which is one class with one set of capabilities and three names. That is a live commercial fact rather than a join key into another system or source, which is why it is not `external_ids` (SPEC §10.1).
product_lineage.title: lineage

product_lineage_entry.description: One party's part in a product's history, and the options that party actually fitted. As-built, never a catalog of what the party offers: a world document is not a product configurator whose rules every consumer would have to reimplement (SPEC §10.1).

designation.description: The product's code in that party's own catalog.

options.description: The options this party applied. An option appears once, on the entry of the party that applied it, so the same fitting is never written twice.

party.description: The organization's name in words; v0 has no entity for an organization.

product_lineage_entry.title: lineage entry

product_lineage_option.description: One fitting, on the entry of the party that applied it. It describes and never rules: what a class can carry, how fast it travels and how big it is stay stated flat on the class, exactly once, so no capability is readable in two places that could disagree (SPEC §10.1).

designation.description: The option's code in the naming party's catalog — the same word as the entry-level field on purpose, because it is one concept at two scales.

detail.description: An open description of the option. It describes; it never restates or overrides the class's own numbers.

name.description: In human words, and required: an option nobody can name is not one.

offered_by.description: Whose catalog the option came out of, when that is somebody other than the party that applied it.

replaces.description: Free text naming the stock item this displaced.

product_lineage_option.title: lineage option

product_lineage_role.description: What a party did to the product. Closed, because the chain runs origin to site and two designations with no direction between them are a rebrand nobody can order (SPEC §10.1).
product_lineage_role.title: lineage role

product_param_decl.description: One knob's declaration. A parameter with no default must be bound by every stamp; leaving one unbound is a load error rather than a silent zero (SPEC §6).
product_param_decl.title: parameter declaration

product_pick.description: A PICK PLACE: where an operator takes goods out of an inventory carrier presented beside them and puts those goods into the carrier an HTM is holding out. It carries no fields — which carrier is held out is said by the `presentation_point` on the same cell, and what is picked is said by the order the carrier belongs to (SPEC §10).
product_pick.title: pick

product_port.description: A boundary point where things enter or leave the world (SPEC §10).

direction.description: Whether the world gains something here or loses it.

from.description: The station a source port draws from.

into.description: The station a sink port feeds.

of.$comment: SPEC §10 describes these entries as carrier-type refs plus a designation; the Dallas catalog writes a carrier kind plus a designation instead, and says why in its own comment. The entry shape is left open until that is ruled — see README.md.
of.description: What passes through, one entry per kind of thing.

product_port.title: port

product_presentation_point.description: Where a carrier is presented to an operator. v0 binds it to a serving cell by proximity; explicit binding is an open question (SPEC §10, §12.11).

attributes.description: The point's presentation geometry as Map Creator states it: the cell it names, the height a carrier is presented at, the robot class that presents it and the heading it presents at, the direction the operator reaches from, and whether the operator works here. The cell is the producer's statement and agrees with the point's pose; whether a point binds a serving cell explicitly stays open (SPEC §12.11).

bot_orientation.description: The heading the robot presents at.

bot_type.description: The robot class that presents a carrier here.

cell.description: The cell this point stands on, as the producer named it.

cell_unresolved.description: The cell the producer named, as it named it, present only where it names no cell the same document declares.

display_attributes.description: How Map Creator labels the point for an operator.

is_workbench.description: Whether this is where the operator works.

pick_direction.description: The direction the operator reaches from.

presentation_height.description: The height a carrier is presented at.

light_curtain.description: Whether an optical safety barrier guards this point, as Map Creator states it.

presented_entity_allowed_types.description: What may be presented here, as Map Creator states it.

presenting_agent_id.description: The robot that presents a carrier here, where the producer names one.

presenting_agent_type.description: The kind of robot that presents a carrier here, as Map Creator states it.

station.description: The station this point belongs to. A producer that nests a station's points inside its record, as Map Creator does, states it here, and the shipped `presentation_cell` lenses read it.

world_coordinates_unresolved.description: The grid coordinates the producer stated for the point, as it stated them, present only where the cell it names is not one the same document declares, so no cell can give them back.

product_presentation_point.title: presentation point

product_queue.description: An ordered path of cells with a discipline — the horseshoe under a station's safety cover, or one approach cell. The path is the admission: every cell on it admits an occupant, and a scenario admitting fewer states a shorter path. A path step must resolve to a live cell; dangling, removed or non-cell targets refuse the load (SPEC §10).

discipline.description: What entering the path commits an agent to. `no_reverse` is the point of no return the sequencing logic must respect.

path.description: The cells in the order they are travelled, named in the one address vocabulary a stitch pair also uses — never bare key strings, which cannot survive outside the entity that coined them. The list is what the queue admits on, so it is also what a policy overlay restates to admit fewer.

product_queue.title: queue

product_repeat.description: Instance i sits at the stamp's position plus i steps. The step is expressed in the frame of the stamp's pose and is deliberately not rotated by the stamp's heading, so a rotated row marches along the same world axis as an unrotated one and the two span the same extent (SPEC §6).
product_repeat.title: repeat

product_sector.description: A shapeless named grouping used as a selector for behaviours — explicit members, or the region beside it, or both. A generator listed as a member stands for its whole expansion (SPEC §10).
product_sector.title: sector

product_stamp.description: One placement of a template, optionally repeated. Expansion always produces an instance level, repeat or not, so adding a repeat later cannot silently rename every identity beneath it (SPEC §6).

params.description: Values bound to the template's parameters, by name. A value may be any JSON the parameter stands for.

product_stamp.title: stamp

product_station.description: A workstation: what it does, and which product it is (SPEC §10).

role.description: The product this station is — `easyloop`, `box_induction`. Open by design: a new station kind is a new template, not a schema change.

product_station.title: station

product_template.description: A reusable sub-world: internal entities named by local handles instead of UUIDs, positioned in the template's own local frame, parameterized where the product varies. A template ships its own internal connectivity, so a site author does not have to wire its organs together (SPEC §6).

entities.description: The entities one instance of this template consists of.

params.description: The knobs this template offers, each by name.

product_template.title: template

product_template_entity.description: One entity inside a template, addressed by its handle. Its components are read exactly as an entity's components are read anywhere else.

components.description: Read exactly as any entity's components are read. The authoring profile reaches in here too — see authoring.json's strict overlay.

name.description: A label for people. Not identity, never unique, never referenced.

product_template_entity.title: template internal

product_waiting.description: A holding pool. Capacity is simply its cell count, so it carries no fields of its own — the region and tiling beside it say how big it is (SPEC §10).
product_waiting.title: waiting

spatial_cell.description: A node an agent can occupy — the thing the traversability graph is built out of. Derived by a tiling or declared by hand, with the same standing either way (SPEC §5).

adjacency.description: The four neighbours a survey states, one slot per direction with an empty slot where there is none: the original form the stitches beside the cell are derived from, which cannot state a one-way lane, an impassable neighbour pair or a grade.

barcode_properties.description: The per-cell robot permissions Map Creator keys by the cell's floor sticker, kept whole.

blocked.description: Something stands here — a building column, a pallet — so nothing may occupy the cell even though it exists.

composite_attribute_list.description: The cell's second, list-valued classification as Map Creator states it.

conveyor_direction_attribute.description: The conveyor direction Map Creator states for this cell.

floor.description: The floor this cell's record names, beside the floor its pose's frame says: Map Creator states it on some cells and not others.

grid_attribute.description: The cell's classification as Map Creator states it, which the orchestrator recomputes for itself.

has_storables.description: Map Creator's `hasStorables`, as it states it: a number, or null.

legacy_grid_coordinate.description: The coordinate a legacy system recorded for this cell, kept because real lattices drift and the declared frame gives only the nominal projection. Data, never identity, never a key (SPEC §4).

location_profile.description: The location profile this cell names: the per-robot-model, per-heading permission table `traversable_by` is the flat reading of, kept whole on the profile entity. Map Creator states it as the profile's id.

location_profile_unresolved.description: The location profile id the producer stated, as it stated it, present only where it names no profile the same document declares — a reference whose target is missing, kept rather than dropped.

neighbours.description: The travel grade toward each of the four neighbours — whether a neighbour exists, whether a robot may move to it, whether it may move there loaded — of which a stitch is the ungraded, two-way reading.

runtime.description: What was happening on this cell when the producer wrote it down: the robot standing on it and why it is blocked. Live state rather than layout, carried so a consumer can drop it on purpose rather than lose it by accident.

botid.description: The robot standing on the cell, or none.

size.description: A hand-declared cell's own extent. A derived cell's is its tile; a declared cell with no size is 900 × 900 mm expressed in the frame's steps — the one physical constant the suffix purge leaves standing, because a default cannot be a step count until a document says what a step is (SPEC §5).

size_info.description: The four half-extents a survey states, of which `size` is the per-axis sum: kept because the sum loses where a footprint that is not centred on the cell lies. In the producer's own unit, millimetres for Map Creator.

special.description: Whether this cell is where a robot re-establishes its position, as Map Creator states it.

store_status.description: Whether a movable rack may be parked on this cell, as Map Creator states it.

traversable_by.description: The agent classes that physically fit here. Capability, not policy: whether traffic is allowed to run this way is `flow`'s business (SPEC §7).

world_coordinate_reference_neighbour.description: The neighbour Map Creator measured this cell's position from.

zone.description: The zone this cell belongs to: the e-stop and light-curtain domain a safety event pauses or blocks whole.

zone_unresolved.description: The zone name the producer stated, as it stated it, present only where it names no zone the same document declares.

spatial_cell.title: cell

spatial_charging.description: A robot charging point. A marker with no fields, declared individually or through a tiling's `derives` (SPEC §5, §10). This denotes charging equipment, not a generic idle destination; charge-state dispatch is a simulator policy.
spatial_charging.title: charging

spatial_exclusion.description: A rectangle a tiling leaves untiled: anchored at its minimum corner, stated relative to its region's origin, in the region's frame's steps. Each derived cell whose centre falls strictly inside it is removed — from this tiling only, so what a tiling derives is a function of the tiling alone (SPEC §5).

origin.description: The minimum corner, measured from the region's own origin. It may sit outside the region, which is how a carve-out authored against a whole floor keeps its geometry when it is written onto one tiling of it.

spatial_exclusion.title: exclusion

spatial_frame.description: A declared coordinate system. One frame per world is primary — 3-D, world-fixed, and the only one that says what a step is worth — and every other frame reaches it through a chain of transforms, so conversion is defined in exactly one place (SPEC §4).

dims.description: How many axes this frame has. The primary frame is 3-D; a floor or a lattice is usually 2-D.

integer_only.description: Positions declared in this frame must be whole numbers; projections into it round half-up and are understood to be approximate (SPEC §4).

parent.description: The frame this one is measured against. Absent on the primary frame and only there.

transform_to_parent.description: How a point in this frame reads in the parent's: `p_parent = translation + scale ⊙ p_frame`, per axis. A negative scale entry is the mirror (SPEC §4).

unit_mm.description: What one integer step of this format's lengths is worth physically. The primary frame declares it and no other frame may, so a step becomes physical in exactly one place (SPEC §4).

units.description: What one step of this frame measures: a length (`mm`, sized by the primary frame's `unit_mm` through the chain) or a lattice index (`index`), whose physical pitch lives in the transform's scale (SPEC §4).

vendor.description: The robot vendor whose install this frame belongs to. A vendor frame is not a kind of frame — just a frame so tagged (SPEC §4).

spatial_frame.title: frame

spatial_pose.description: Where an entity sits, and optionally which way it faces, in a stated frame. Inside a template the frame is absent: the pose is in the template's own local frame and acquires a frame when a stamp places it (SPEC §5).

heading_deg.description: Counter-clockwise from +x. An angle is not a length and takes its unit from no frame, so it keeps its suffix and may be fractional.

spatial_pose.title: pose

spatial_region.description: A rectangle in a frame, anchored at its minimum corner and measured in that frame's steps. Declaring one in a frame whose units are `index` is a load error: an integer lattice frame is for projecting into, never for authoring in (SPEC §5).

size.description: Extent from the origin. Each extent must be a positive whole multiple of the matching tiling pitch — no silent remainder strips (SPEC §5).

spatial_region.title: region

spatial_tiling.description: What makes a region a cell_grid: derive a cell per tile at this pitch, each carrying the whole component map in `derives` (SPEC §5). Tiling is opt-in per region — a real site tiles the strips robots actually travel, not its whole floor.

derives.description: Every component each derived cell carries, verbatim — which is how an area-level fact is declared once instead of per cell: these cells admit HTMs, these cells have chargers. A cell whose `derives` names no `cell` component still carries an empty one.

exclusions.description: The parts of its own region this tiling leaves untiled. A tiling states its own holes, so no other entity has to reach into this one to punch them and a hole meant for one tiling cannot take cells out of another that overlaps it (SPEC §5). Absent means none.

pitch.description: Tile size, which is also each derived cell's footprint.

spatial_tiling.title: tiling

spatial_transform.description: The per-axis translation and scale that carry a point from one frame into its parent. A 2-D frame under a 3-D parent embeds as [x, y] → [x, y, 0] before translating, which is why its translation carries three entries and its scale two (SPEC §4).
spatial_transform.title: transform to parent

structure_access.description: The junction between a run of racking and the region it is worked from: this run, that region, this face, these classes. Four fields are the whole of it and it derives nothing at all — it is a statement, and the SPEC §7 checks and the motion model are its consumers, which is what makes a world expand identically whether or not a fleet is layered over it (SPEC §5).

along.description: The region this face is worked from — a cell_grid where the classes that work it drive, a plain untiled region where they climb.

face.description: The face storage is reached from — the one place in the format that states a side. Where a relay stands is geometry on its own level, because in a rack | aisle | rack zone the two are opposite.

rack.description: The run: a stamp whose instances are the bays.

serves.description: The robot classes that work this face. Absent means unrestricted.

structure_access.title: access

structure_access_cell.description: The binding: the one cell an HTM occupies to exchange with this relay. Nothing is minted for it — it names an ordinary cell of the cell_grid the HTM travels, found by the binding search or stated by an override, which are the same component either way (SPEC §5).
structure_access_cell.title: access cell

structure_direction.description: Which way along an axis traffic runs.
structure_direction.title: direction

structure_flow.description: Which way traffic runs inside one generator's cells — a policy statement, not a physical one. A cell_grid with no flow compiles two-way: flow restricts, never permits (SPEC §5, §7).

then.description: Both of these rules run traffic a stated way, so the direction is not optional for them.

structure_flow.title: flow

structure_flow_rule.description: How a direction turns into arcs: `one_way` emits along-axis arcs the stated way only, with crossings to the next row still two-way; `two_way` emits every orthogonal-neighbour arc both ways; `alternating_rows` alternates each row, even rows running the stated way (SPEC §5).
structure_flow_rule.title: flow rule

structure_level.description: One entry of a rack's `levels`: a height, and either the relays that protrude from it or the storage it holds — never both. An entry carrying `positions` is a relay level; one without is a storage level; and both key forms index the full list, so inserting a relay level renumbers nothing (SPEC §5).

height.description: How far above the floor at the rack's pose this shelf sits.

positions.description: Where this level's shelves stand, each an `[along, out]` offset from the bay's origin corner in the bay's own frame. Which side of the steel a shelf protrudes on is the second number — at or below zero for the low-`y` face, at or beyond the footprint's depth for the high-`y` one — so the side is geometry and not an enum. Stating them is what makes this a relay level.

reach.description: How far from a relay of this level a cell may sit and still be the one it binds. A radius around the shelf: the binding search asks proximity and nothing else.

then.description: The offsets place the shelves on their own, but nothing says how far one may reach for a cell, so a relay level states a reach.

structure_level.title: level

structure_rack.description: One bay of racking: pure steel, and nothing about who serves it. Its vertical truth is one enumerated list of levels, bottom-up, because real bays are not uniformly spaced and a nominal pitch would be a second number that could disagree with the survey. It derives one relay per position of every relay level and one slot per storage position. A rack reachable from both sides is one rack with two accesses, not two logical racks (SPEC §5).

footprint.description: Extent at heading 0, anchored with its minimum corner at the rack's pose (SPEC §5).

levels.description: Every shelf this bay has, enumerated bottom-up. Heights increase down the list, and a list that does not increase is a load error: `the lowest level` and `level 3` both have to mean one thing. There is no level pitch and no level count (SPEC §5).

slot_pitch.description: Along-face and depth spacing of storage positions.

slots_deep.description: How deep storage goes from the access face — 2 is double-deep, where the rear position is reachable only after the front carrier moves.

structure_rack.title: rack

structure_relay.description: One handoff shelf, where carriers change hands between the rack system and the floor. It names the rack and the level it stands on, how high that is and where on the bay it sits — not the cell somebody stands on, which is the `access_cell` beside it (SPEC §5).

index.description: Which of that level's positions this is, in the order they are written.

level.description: Which entry of the rack's `levels` this shelf stands on, zero-based.

offset.description: The entry of its level's `positions` that derived it: `[along, out]` from the bay's origin corner, in the bay's own frame. An offset, not a world position — the rack's pose carries it into a frame.

structure_relay.title: relay

structure_side.description: Which face of a bay is meant, stated in the run template's own frame; the stamp's heading turns it like all stamped geometry. Only an access states one.
structure_side.title: side

structure_slot.description: One storage position of a rack, individually addressable so a stored carrier, a damaged position, or a double-deep front/rear pair can be named. Depth counts from the access face, which is what makes front and rear mean anything (SPEC §5).

col.description: Storage column across the face, zero-based.

depth.description: How far back from the access face, zero-based.

level.description: Which entry of the rack's `levels` this shelf is, zero-based.

structure_slot.title: slot

structure_stitch.description: A declared linking rule between two expansions' cells. Nothing links without one — two cell_grids that touch are two cell_grids that touch, never an implicit merge (SPEC §5).

a.description: One endpoint. Any entity whose expansion contributes cells will do — a region, a stamp.

pairs.$comment: Not `required` when the rule is explicit, because the reader does not require it either: an explicit stitch with no pairs silently links nothing there. Raised as an open question in README.md rather than settled here.
pairs.description: The cells an explicit rule links, two per pair, in the one address vocabulary a queue path also uses.

tolerance.description: How far apart two cells may be and still be linked by a contact rule; overlap counts as zero.

structure_stitch.title: stitch

structure_stitch_rule.description: How the two endpoints' cells are matched: `contact` links each cell of the smaller expansion to its nearest partner within tolerance, many-to-one by design; `explicit` links exactly the stated pairs, used where contact would be wrong — a station's only legal entry, a threshold, a directional gate (SPEC §5).
structure_stitch_rule.title: stitch rule

structure_storage.description: What a rack or buffer may hold. Two racks of identical steel differ only in this: the order buffer is the inventory rack template with `holds` replaced (SPEC §10).

carrier_type.description: The carrier type this storage takes, where it takes only one.

holds.description: Which side of the operation this steel serves.

structure_storage.title: storage

values_axis_vector.description: One number per axis of a frame — two entries, or three where a 2-D frame embeds in a 3-D parent and the third entry is its elevation (SPEC §4).
values_axis_vector.title: axis vector

values_cell_address.description: How anything names one cell: by its own identity — a declared cell's UUID or a derived cell's address, the two being equally valid here — by that derived address written in its two parts, or, inside a template only, by a local one. Never a bare key string, which would only mean something to whichever entity coined it (SPEC §3).
values_cell_address.title: cell address

values_coord.description: One axis of a position, in the steps of the frame that states it (SPEC §5).
values_coord.title: coordinate

values_coord_pair.description: Two coordinates in the frame of whatever states them, x then y.
values_coord_pair.title: coordinate pair

values_count.description: How many of something, zero included.
values_count.title: count

values_count_positive.description: How many of something, where none of it would be meaningless.
values_count_positive.title: positive count

values_declared_entity_id.description: The identity of an entity somebody wrote down: a freshly minted UUID meaning nothing but "this one" (SPEC §3). This is the one identity in the format that is a real UUID.
values_declared_entity_id.title: declared entity id

values_derivation_address.description: The complete address of one derived entity, in the two parts a record writes it in: the declared generator the chain starts at, and the key that walks down from it. This is the same identity `derived_entity_id` spells flat, and a record addresses a derived entity by it (SPEC §3).
values_derivation_address.title: derivation address

values_derivation_key.description: The `/`-joined chain of segments naming one derived entity beneath its generator. Every segment carries a reserved prefix and a non-empty payload; a payload keeps its own colons, so `local:present:0` is the handle `present:0` (SPEC §3).
values_derivation_key.title: derivation key

values_derived_entity_id.description: The identity of an entity a generator produced: the address it was produced at — the declared generator's UUID, then the `/`-joined key that walks down to it, `6f1c…/instance:2/relay:1,0`. The address IS the identity, with nothing computed underneath it; two implementations name the same entity because they walked the same chain (SPEC §3). This is the flat spelling, which is what an `id` field and a database key hold; `derivation_address` below is the same address written in the two parts a record addresses one by.
values_derived_entity_id.title: derived entity id

values_entity_id.description: The identity of one entity, either way it was minted: a UUID for a declared entity, a derivation address for a derived one. The two arms record HOW a name came about and never a kind of entity — derivation is a convenience and never a second class of existence (SPEC §1, §3) — so every field that names an entity takes either arm, and nothing may treat one differently once it has resolved it.
values_entity_id.title: entity id

values_entity_ref.description: A pointer at another entity: an identity out in the world — a declared entity's UUID or a derived entity's address, either is valid here — and a local handle inside a template. A dangling one is a load error, never a best-effort match (SPEC §2).
values_entity_ref.title: entity reference

values_flag.description: A yes-or-no fact about an entity.
values_flag.title: flag

values_local_derivation_address.description: A derivation address written inside a template, where the generator is still a handle; expansion rewrites it into a plain derivation address (SPEC §3).
values_local_derivation_address.title: local derivation address

values_local_handle.description: A template-internal entity's name, standing in for an identity until a stamp mints one. `/` is forbidden inside it because `/` joins derivation key segments (SPEC §3).
values_local_handle.title: local handle

values_local_ref.description: How one template internal names another before either has an identity; expansion rewrites it to the stamped identity (SPEC §2).
values_local_ref.title: local reference

values_param_ref.description: A template parameter standing where a value goes; substitution replaces the whole object with the bound value, preserving its JSON type (SPEC §6). Partial-string interpolation does not exist.
values_param_ref.title: parameter reference

values_position.description: A point in a frame: two entries in a 2-D frame, three in a 3-D one (SPEC §4).
values_position.title: position

values_steps.description: A length: an integer count of the steps of the frame it is stated in. Only the primary frame's `unit_mm` says what a step is worth, which is why no length field carries a unit in its name any more (SPEC §5).
values_steps.title: steps

values_steps_list.description: Lengths in a stated order, as many as the thing has.
values_steps_list.title: step list

values_steps_pair.description: Two lengths, x then y, in the steps of the frame that states them.
values_steps_pair.title: step pair

values_steps_pair_list.description: Offsets in a stated order, each a pair of lengths in the steps of the frame that states them.
values_steps_pair_list.title: step pair list

values_steps_pair_positive.description: Two lengths that must both exceed zero: a size, a pitch, a footprint.
values_steps_pair_positive.title: positive step pair

values_steps_positive.description: A length that must be greater than zero: an extent, a pitch, a footprint side.
values_steps_positive.title: positive steps

values_unit_mm.description: What one integer step is worth physically — the only fractional number a geometry document carries, declared by the primary frame and by no other (SPEC §4, §5). 0.1 is the expected site default, because source drawings carry tenths of a millimetre and a tenth is finer than anything a warehouse holds to.
values_unit_mm.title: step size in millimetres

values_uuid.description: A UUID in the hyphenated form. SPEC §3 writes identities lowercase; a reader accepts either case, so this does too.
values_uuid.title: UUID

schema.description: What makes a region a cell_grid: derive a cell per tile at this pitch, each carrying the whole component map in `derives` (SPEC §5). Tiling is opt-in per region — a real site tiles the strips robots actually travel, not its whole floor.

derives.description: Every component each derived cell carries, verbatim — which is how an area-level fact is declared once instead of per cell: these cells admit HTMs, these cells have chargers. A cell whose `derives` names no `cell` component still carries an empty one.

exclusions.description: The parts of its own region this tiling leaves untiled. A tiling states its own holes, so no other entity has to reach into this one to punch them and a hole meant for one tiling cannot take cells out of another that overlaps it (SPEC §5). Absent means none.

pitch.description: Tile size, which is also each derived cell's footprint.

schema.title: tiling
